subject: docs/coop/artifacts/coordinator-decisions.D-100.turn3.draft.md
summary: Independent attack found no MUST-FIX or SHOULD-FIX. D100-T2-MF-1 is landed with candidate-keyed grant coverage and a determinate Product + release + platform test for the non-row Windows candidate; ADV-D100-01 remains closed by the exactly-one-row rule for the shared 106/109/113 draft. The entry remains mechanics only, requires a separate prior user-made grant, excludes D-054/D-057 as that grant, does not generalize DR-116 Route C, and produces no SATISFIED, file-08, implementation, or readiness effect. All cited identities match live bytes, and the frozen subject, prompt, turn-1 subject, and turn-2 subject remained unchanged.

attack_results.attack: D100-T2-MF-1 not landed (Windows still has no determinate grant-coverage test)
attack_results.evidence: Decision item 1 keys D-096(A) to every named role for the candidate (lines 40-46), and the operative precondition repeats candidate-keying before distinguishing row-backed candidates from Windows (lines 52-58). The eligibility table names Windows' complete coverage set as Product + release + platform (line 80); required pins expressly require no file-08 row for Windows but do require the owner roles being recorded (lines 101-107); and the allowed-effect clause records the named non-row platform set (lines 120-125). These match live deferral.windows-platform.preview.v2.json fields ownerWhoMustRecord and condition2EffectIfOwnerRecorded.

The special rule requires exactly one selected row, the selected row's full role set, and a separate D-000 cycle and commit for each row; acting on one has no effect on the other two (lines 86-95). The required pins repeat exactly one selected row (lines 101-105), and the effect rule expressly forbids bundling (lines 124-132).

attack_results.attack: Treats this as a grant or treats D-054 / D-057 as covering these rows
attack_results.evidence: The header says mechanics only, no grant, D-096(A) unsatisfied, and no D-054/D-057 invocation (lines 9-16). Decision items 1-2 require a later, applicable, ADOPTED user-made grant and forbid citing D-054/D-057 as it (lines 40-59); every later owner entry must state that D-054/D-057 are not the path (lines 97-110). The rejected alternatives and readiness section preserve the same boundary (lines 138-142 and 156-159).

Decision item 1 expressly says a mechanics entry alone never grants (lines 40-46). The later owner record has conjunctive preconditions: live D-096, live D-100, and a separately adopted, non-overturned user grant covering every candidate role (lines 48-69). Reversibility also states that D-100 creates or revokes no grant (lines 161-167).

The candidate table confines Route C to DR-116's Product security role (line 78), the scope exclusions expressly say DR-116 Route C does not generalize (lines 82-84), and the alternatives reject generalization by reference to D-096 (line 148). The universal user-grant precondition still applies to DR-116 and every other eligible candidate.

The header denies any SATISFIED effect (lines 8 and 13); the candidate scope denies a SATISFIED re-record (lines 82-84); and the operative effect rule forbids marking any row SATISFIED, reserving any future MF-6 to its own later D-000 review (lines 120-128). This entry records no row and has zero readiness effect (line 134 and lines 156-159).

The header says this entry does not edit file 08 (line 14), the operative effect rule prohibits a later owner-recording from editing it (line 126), and the alternative is expressly rejected (line 149). Live file 08 remained at the cited digest.

The header denies implementation authorization (line 12), the operative effect rule repeats that prohibition (line 129), the alternative is rejected because condition 5 remains last (line 154), and the readiness section leaves condition 5 last (lines 156-159).
